description: Authored before the comparison run; small diagnostic retrieval set, not a held-out benchmark or production corpus. Every query has exactly one relevant document. No labels or texts may be tuned after viewing results.

documents.title: Restore a backup
documents.text: To recover a deleted database, stop the application and restore last night's backup into a new directory. Validate the recovered records before switching the application to that directory. A restore recovers data; creating a snapshot does not recover an already deleted record.

documents.title: Backup retention policy
documents.text: Keep seven daily backups and four weekly backups. Delete older backup archives only after the newest archive passes its integrity check. Retention controls how long recovery copies are stored, rather than how a database is restored.

documents.title: Virtual machine snapshots
documents.text: Take a virtual machine snapshot before upgrading the operating system. A snapshot provides a quick rollback point for that machine, but it does not replace an off-machine backup. Delete the temporary snapshot after validating the upgrade.

documents.title: GTE text chunking
documents.text: GTE-small accepts at most 512 WordPiece tokens including CLS and SEP. Split long documents into overlapping chunks before embedding them. The tokenizer lowercases ASCII text. This limit concerns input length, not the 384-dimensional output vector.

documents.title: Gemma attention window
documents.text: EmbeddingGemma uses bidirectional local attention with an inclusive radius of 512 token positions. Every sixth layer uses full attention. Its embedding API allows 8192 input tokens including the query or document prefix and BOS and EOS. A local attention window is not the total input context limit.

documents.title: Shorter embedding vectors
documents.text: Matryoshka embeddings can be shortened by taking a prefix of the output vector. Renormalise that prefix to unit length before cosine search. Reducing the output dimension saves vector storage, but it does not shorten the input or remove transformer layers.

documents.title: CPU-only embedding worker
documents.text: The NAS embedding worker runs native Go inference on CPU. It has no GPU dependency and uses AVX2 when supported. Limit simultaneous requests to avoid consuming all processor capacity. A GPU is not required for this worker.

documents.title: GPU training workstation
documents.text: The training workstation uses a GPU to fine-tune models. Check GPU memory capacity and driver compatibility before starting a training job. These training requirements do not describe the separate CPU-only inference worker.

documents.title: Rotate an API token
documents.text: Create a replacement API token with the same minimum permissions. Install the replacement in the secret store, verify authenticated requests, then revoke the old token. Never write API tokens into source files or command logs.

documents.title: Renew an HTTPS certificate
documents.text: An expired TLS certificate prevents clients from establishing a trusted HTTPS connection. Renew the server certificate and install its full certificate chain. Reload the web server and check the new expiry date. Rotating an API token will not repair an expired TLS certificate.

documents.title: Diagnose connection timeouts
documents.text: A connection timeout can result from a firewall rule, an unreachable address or a service that is not listening. Check routing, the destination port and firewall logs. Do not disable TLS certificate validation to diagnose an unreachable server.

documents.title: Refresh missing embeddings
documents.text: When documents have missing or stale embeddings, enqueue a semantic refresh. The background worker processes only the affected documents and updates the vector index. Enabling refresh on startup lets a later restart resume missing work without deleting existing vectors.

documents.title: Lexical document search
documents.text: Lexical search ranks documents using matching terms and a text index. It can find an exact identifier without requiring an embedding model. Rebuilding the lexical index does not regenerate stale semantic vectors.

documents.title: Find a CPU hotspot
documents.text: Capture a CPU profile while repeatedly running a representative workload. Inspect functions with high cumulative and flat CPU time. Optimise measured repeated work, then rerun the same workload to verify elapsed time and correctness.

documents.title: Find allocation churn
documents.text: Use allocation profiles to identify functions that repeatedly allocate temporary objects. Inspect both allocated bytes and object counts. A live heap snapshot measures retained objects and cannot substitute for allocation history. Reuse bounded caller-owned scratch buffers when appropriate.

documents.title: Customer statement of work
documents.text: A statement of work defines customer deliverables, exclusions, milestones, acceptance criteria and responsibilities. Agree those boundaries before staffing delivery. An internal status meeting does not replace customer acceptance criteria.

documents.title: Estimate a cloud deployment
documents.text: Estimate an Azure deployment by listing resource sizes, regions, expected usage and monthly prices. Separate one-time implementation effort from recurring cloud charges. Record pricing assumptions and exclude taxes unless explicitly requested.

documents.title: Internal project meeting
documents.text: The internal project meeting records current progress, decisions, risks and named action owners. Publish the minutes after the meeting. It is an operational update, not a customer contract or a cloud cost estimate.

workloads.name: paragraph
workloads.text: The semantic search worker reads documents, splits their contents into bounded overlapping chunks and generates an embedding for each chunk. Missing or stale vectors are refreshed in the background. The service keeps the existing index available during this work and checks cancellation before publishing new output. Operators should measure representative CPU workloads before changing concurrency limits.

workloads.name: long-chunk
workloads.text: A production service needs a recovery procedure that can be tested independently of the running deployment. Backups must preserve the data, configuration and access policy needed to restore service. Before changing the active model, validate a separate candidate with a fixed set of inputs. Measure load time, warm inference latency, allocation counts and peak memory on the intended host. Compare retrieval rankings against relevance labels written before inspecting the model outputs. Keep the existing worker and vector index available while the candidate is evaluated. A faster kernel does not necessarily make the complete request faster, because tokenisation, attention and memory allocation also contribute to elapsed time. Reuse bounded scratch buffers, honour cancellation and avoid silently truncating documents when the input limit is exceeded. A process using mapped weights may have a small initial heap while its resident memory grows as pages are touched. Record both the retained heap and the process resident memory. Test shorter vectors by renormalising the retained prefix before cosine search. Preserve independent reference checks whenever an optimisation changes numerical reduction order. After the experiment finishes, remove temporary profiles, expanded weights and build artifacts, keeping the source, original checkpoint and concise measured conclusions. Deployment still requires a separate decision based on retrieval quality, operational limits and the target machine's resource budget.
